ideas.risks: The desired theorem may be false; even if true, the two-arm result may not lift to many dyadic windows without losing comparator-specific delay dependence.
ideas.summary: Settle the two-arm delayed-advantage game. Either prove an algorithm with A_T >= -tilde O(sqrt T) and A_T >= S_T - tilde O(sqrt(TD)), perhaps using a reserve/fractional-wealth potential, or build a crisp adversarial advantage sequence refuting comparator-specific delay regret.
ideas.title: Two-Arm Delayed Advantage
ideas.why_promising: This is the minimal unresolved abstraction behind tail-adaptive truncation. A positive result would upgrade the fixed-H upper bound to an oracle over H; a negative result would explain why adaptive truncation is fundamentally harder.

ideas.risks: Information constraints may force exactly the weak one-block lower bound already known. Persistent quotes can also break the intended tail envelope unless quote levels or barriers are engineered carefully.
suggested_lenses: Le Cam or Fano lower bound
ideas.summary: Analyze a limited-leakage common-parameter construction: many blocks share a hidden type, each block has q-mass delayed payoff separation gamma, and terminal observations reveal only small KL or TV information. Compute the finite-grid Bayes value first, then check whether the realized price process preserves beta, Delta, or delta envelopes.
ideas.title: Limited-Leakage Lower Rates
ideas.why_promising: The current q-scaled atom is too weak for power-tail matching because one reveal or independent-bit averaging collapses regret. A noisy common parameter is the most direct way to accumulate hidden value without immediate full learning.

ideas.risks: The best fixed quote may still collapse to a mixture action, or old quotes may trade on later spikes and destroy locality. The construction may need many delicate level separations.
ideas.summary: Try a multi-quote codebook lower bound instead of two fixed quotes. Worlds choose one optimal quote from a packed grid; delayed spikes are arranged so one fixed quote has high value across many unresolved components while posterior uncertainty remains large. Verify Bayes gap, comparator value, and cross-trade tails explicitly.
ideas.title: Codebook Comparator Construction
ideas.why_promising: Independent hidden bits fail because a single two-quote comparator only gains fluctuation size. A codebook might let the best fixed quote encode a global type and accumulate larger regret.

ideas.risks: The resulting object may simply repackage the minimax value or Bayes gap, not give a simpler structural condition. Hidden/labeled examples rule out any condition that ignores public observability.
ideas.summary: Use the last-exceedance identity sum_t r_t(a) = a(L_a - 1)_+ to define value-weighted and predictability-aware tail quantities. Test whether a conditional last-exceedance truncation gap can separate predictable long delays from genuinely hidden delayed value and recover the accepted delta upper bound as a special case.
ideas.title: Predictable Last-Exceedance Tails
ideas.why_promising: First-hitting beta is the wrong raw object. Last exceedances directly govern fixed-quote comparator value, so this may produce a cleaner structural language for tail conditions.

ideas.risks: This may produce theorem hygiene rather than new regret rates. Natural Borel gaps may not exist beyond pathological measurability examples.
ideas.summary: Find useful no-gap hypotheses beyond payoff-measure domination. Prove identifiable Borel classes are easy under measurable decoding, prove dominated-approximation constants, or construct a Borel nondominated non-identifiable infinite class where finite subclasses are easy but the full class has linear value.
ideas.title: Natural Infinite-Class No-Gap
ideas.why_promising: The finite-prior Bayes characterization becomes useful for infinite classes only under no-gap assumptions. Current domination assumptions are sufficient but too restrictive and not necessary.

ideas.risks: The problem may be outside the main horizon-aware minimax regime, and a standard doubling or mixture-over-horizons trick might remove the obstruction.
ideas.summary: Formalize the anytime known-law boundary. Use super-growing deterministic blocks with two candidate deadlines to prove that no single horizon-free known-law policy has sublinear regret on all horizons, or find an anytime construction matching the horizon-aware oracle up to sublinear loss.
ideas.title: Anytime Known-Law Boundary
ideas.why_promising: Known finite-horizon laws are trivially oracle-learnable, so any nontrivial fixed-law necessity must change quantifiers. The anytime version is the cleanest nearby regime where tail structure may matter again.

ideas.risks: The bridge may close cleanly but still not solve the original tail/rate problem. The main danger is accidentally proving only a completed-kernel statement while claiming an original Borel-policy theorem.
ideas.summary: Close or falsify the Borel-policy payoff-domination bridge by proving both reward-set inclusions C_Borel subset C_Linfty and C_Linfty subset C_Borel under the exact finite-grid public-exogenous seed/state model. Track Borel versions, section integrals, finite-action randomization, and null-set caveats.
ideas.title: Borel Bridge Closure
ideas.why_promising: This would turn the completed-kernel no-gap theorem into a referee-ready original-policy theorem under narrow assumptions, eliminating a persistent technical gap in the accepted theorem package.
